basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'VERS. 1.-- | Igitur Joseph ductus in Egyptum, emitque cum Puliphar, eunuchus Pharaonis.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1.-- | Igitur Joseph ductus in Egyptum, emitque cum Puliphar, eunuchus Pharaonis. Ubi quaeritur quomodo postea uxorem habere dicatur? Tradunt Hebraei emptum ab hoc Joseph ob nimiam pulchritudinem in turpe ministerium, et a Domino viribus ejus arefactis, postea electum esse juxta morem Hierophantarum in pontificatum Heliopoleos, et hujus filiam esse Asenec [Z., Asanez], quam postea Joseph uxorem acceperit.
